In evaluating our ability to continue as a going concern for the twelve months following the issuance of these unaudited consolidated financial statements, management projects compliance with these financial covenants.

However, the risks associated with variability in our operating performance could affect management’s forecast and whether we are able to maintain compliance with the maximum total leverage ratio covenant over the next year.

Management has developed plans intended to mitigate these downside risk conditions, including optimization of the Company's distribution and fulfillment network, reductions in cost of goods sold, reductions in marketing spend and other fixed operating costs, and prioritization of available cash towards debt and other obligations.

Accordingly, the plans to mitigate these downside risk conditions do not fully alleviate the substantial doubt about our ability to continue as a going concern for at least the twelve months following the issuance of these unaudited consolidated financial statements.

If we do not achieve the expected benefits from these operational initiatives or if operating results or liquidity deteriorate, we could be required to seek additional capital through equity or debt financing or other sources.
Similarly, there can be no assurance that we will be able to refinance or restructure its debt, or execute any further cost savings or operational improvements.
